source.test: refreshDiscoveredMods -- jarURLs.map has no de-dup step

notes: MSC 1's refreshDiscoveredMods (line 163, jarURLs.map { ... }) has no de-dup step at all -- two jars whose real fabric.mod.json both declare modId 'worldedit' (a user with two copies of the same mod, an old and a new build, both still on disk) still produce two separate ModEntry rows rather than being merged or one being silently dropped. displayName is deliberately distinct between the two ('(new build)'/'(old build)') so the scanner's own sort-by-displayName ordering is deterministic for this fixture's own assertion, not because the scenario requires it -- match_installed_mod (crash_analysis.rs) would attribute a startup problem naming 'worldedit' to whichever entry .find() reaches first, a pre-existing ambiguity this scanner doesn't need to resolve, only to not make worse by hiding one copy.
